title: Hikoya qilish va tajriba bilan bo‘lishish
goal_uz: Dars oxirida siz bir-ikki daqiqalik shaxsiy hikoyani aniq tuzilma (hook, fon, burilish nuqtasi, xulosa), to‘g‘ri o‘tgan zamonlar va his-tuyg‘u so‘zlari bilan aytib berasiz, boshqalarning hikoyasiga esa kamida to‘rt xil tabiiy munosabat bildirasiz.

scenes.title: Bugun: tajribani qiziqarli aytib berish
board: Telling stories in English
Structure · Sequence · Feelings · Reactions
scenes.say_native: Assalomu alaykum! Oldingi darsda eng ko‘p uchraydigan o‘ttizta xatoni tozaladik. Bugun hikoya qilishni o‘rganamiz: dushanba kungi suhbatda, ish intervyusida va IELTS ning ikkinchi qismida aynan shu ko‘nikma kerak. Dars oxirida bir-ikki daqiqalik shaxsiy hikoyani aniq tuzilma va his-tuyg‘ular bilan aytasiz, boshqalarning hikoyasiga esa tabiiy munosabat bildirasiz.
scenes.say: Welcome back! Today is all about stories: how to tell a real experience well, and how to react to other people’s stories.
scenes.say_uz: Qaytganingiz bilan! Bugun hammasi hikoyalar haqida: haqiqiy tajribani qanday yaxshi aytib berish va boshqalarning hikoyalariga qanday munosabat bildirish.

scenes.title: Hikoyaning skeleti
board: 1 Hook (diqqatni tortadigan birinchi gap)
2 Background: who, where, when (fon)
3 Problem → turning point (burilish)
4 Resolution + point (yechim va xulosa)
scenes.say_native: Yaxshi hikoyaning skeleti bor. Avval hook, ya’ni tinglovchini qiziqtiradigan birinchi gap. Keyin qisqa fon: kim, qayerda, qachon. So‘ng muammo va hammasi o‘zgaradigan burilish nuqtasi. Oxirida yechim va xulosa: bu voqeadan nima o‘rgandingiz yoki u nega kulgili edi.
scenes.say: A good story has a shape: a hook, the background, a problem with a turning point, and finally the resolution and the point.
scenes.say_uz: Yaxshi hikoyaning shakli bor: hook, fon, burilish nuqtasi bilan muammo va oxirida yechim hamda xulosa.

scenes.title: Namuna hikoya: o‘chib qolgan proyektor
board: The projector story
Find: the hook, the problem, the point
scenes.say_native: Endi qisqa namuna hikoyani tinglang. Gapiruvchi birinchi katta taqdimotida bo‘lgan voqeani aytib beradi. Uchta narsani toping: hikoya qaysi gap bilan boshlanadi, muammo qayerda paydo bo‘ladi va oxirida qanday xulosa chiqariladi. Zamonlarga ham quloq soling, ularni keyin tahlil qilamiz.
scenes.say: I’ll never forget my first big presentation. It was a Monday morning, and twenty managers were sitting in the room. I had prepared for weeks. I was just starting my second slide when the projector suddenly died. The room went completely silent, and my heart was pounding. So I picked up a marker and drew my main chart on the whiteboard. In the end, my boss said it was the clearest talk of the day. Since then, I’ve always had a plan B.
scenes.say_uz: Birinchi katta taqdimotimni hech qachon unutmayman. Dushanba ertalab edi, xonada yigirmata menejer o‘tirgan edi. Men bir necha hafta tayyorlangan edim. Endigina ikkinchi slaydni boshlayotgan edim, proyektor birdan o‘chib qoldi. Xona butunlay jim bo‘lib qoldi, yuragim gupillab urardi. Shunda markerni olib, asosiy grafigimni doskaga chizdim. Oxir-oqibat rahbarim bu kunning eng tushunarli chiqishi bo‘ldi dedi. O‘shandan beri menda doim zaxira reja bor.

scenes.title: Namunani tahlil qilamiz
board: Hook: I’ll never forget my first big presentation.
Background: Monday morning, twenty managers
Turning point: the projector suddenly died
Point: Since then, I’ve always had a plan B.
scenes.say_native: Tahlil qilamiz. “I’ll never forget my first big presentation” bu hook. Dushanba ertalab va yigirmata menejer haqidagi gaplar fon. “The projector suddenly died” burilish nuqtasi. Doskadagi grafik yechim, oxirgi gap esa xulosa. Hikoya bir daqiqaga ham yetmaydi, lekin unda hamma qism bor.
scenes.say: Notice how short it is: a hook, a little background, one dramatic moment, a quick solution and a final point.
scenes.say_uz: Qanchalik qisqa ekaniga e’tibor bering: hook, ozgina fon, bitta keskin lahza, tezkor yechim va yakuniy xulosa.

scenes.title: Hikoyani qanday boshlash mumkin
board: You won’t believe what happened to me last week.
Did I ever tell you about the time I…?
Something really funny happened at work today.
I’ll never forget the day I…

examples.t: Did I ever tell you about the time I got locked in the office?
examples.uz: Ofisda qamalib qolganimni hech aytib berganmidim?

examples.t: You won’t believe what happened at the airport.

scenes.say_native: Mana tayyor hooklar. Ular tinglovchiga “hozir qiziq narsa aytiladi” degan signal beradi. “Did I ever tell you about the time…” do‘stona, norasmiy ohang. “I’ll never forget the day…” jiddiyroq, intervyu va IELTS uchun ham mos. Ularni yod oling, chunki hikoyada eng qiyini boshlash.
scenes.say: You won’t believe what happened to me last week. Did I ever tell you about the time I got locked in the office? I’ll never forget the day I started my first job.
scenes.say_uz: O‘tgan hafta boshimga nima tushganiga ishonmaysiz. Ofisda qamalib qolganimni hech aytib berganmidim? Birinchi ishimni boshlagan kunimni hech qachon unutmayman.

scenes.title: Tuzilmadagi odatiy xatolar
board: ✗ I want to tell you a story about my trip.
✓ You won’t believe what happened on my trip.
✗ … and that’s all. (birdan to‘xtash)
✓ Anyway, what I learned was…
scenes.say_native: O‘zbek tilida biz ko‘pincha “Bir kuni…” deb boshlab, juda uzoq fon beramiz. Ingliz tinglovchisi esa tezroq asosiy voqeaga o‘tishni kutadi. Yana ikki xato: hikoyani rasmiy e’londek “I want to tell you a story about…” deb boshlash va birdan “That’s all” deb to‘xtatish. Yaxshisi “Anyway…” deb xulosaga o‘ting.
scenes.say: Don’t announce your story like a speech, and don’t stop with that’s all. Close with a clear point: Anyway, what I learned was to always check the date twice.
scenes.say_uz: Hikoyangizni nutqdek e’lon qilmang va “bo‘ldi, shu” deb to‘xtamang. Aniq xulosa bilan yoping: Xullas, men sanani doim ikki marta tekshirishni o‘rgandim.

scenes.title: Mashq: hikoyani tartibga keltiring
board: a) In the end, we got there just in time.
b) Did I ever tell you about my sister’s wedding?
c) Halfway there, our car broke down.
d) We were driving to the venue, already late.
scenes.say_native: Doskada to‘rtta gap aralash berilgan. Ularni hikoya tartibida joylashtiring: hook, fon, burilish nuqtasi, yechim. Signal so‘zlarga qarang: savol shaklidagi gap, “halfway there”, “in the end”. Tartibni harflar bilan baland ovozda ayting, keyin butun hikoyani bir marta o‘qib chiqing.
scenes.say: Put the four sentences in the right order to make a story. Look for the hook, the background, the problem and the ending.
scenes.say_uz: To‘rtta gapni to‘g‘ri tartibga solib, hikoya tuzing. Hook, fon, muammo va yakunni toping.

scenes.title: Javob: b, d, c, a
board: b) Hook: Did I ever tell you about…?
d) Background: We were driving…, already late.
c) Turning point: our car broke down.
a) Resolution: In the end, we got there just in time.
scenes.say_native: To‘g‘ri tartib: b, d, c, a. Savol shaklidagi gap hook. “We were driving…” past continuous, ya’ni fon. “Our car broke down” past simple bilan berilgan keskin voqea, burilish nuqtasi. “In the end” uzoq kutilgan yakunni bildiradi. Ko‘rdingizmi, zamonlarning o‘zi tartibni ko‘rsatib turibdi.
scenes.say: Did I ever tell you about my sister’s wedding? We were driving to the venue, already late. Halfway there, our car broke down. In the end, we got there just in time.
scenes.say_uz: Opamning to‘yi haqida hech aytib berganmidim? To‘yxonaga mashinada ketayotgan edik, allaqachon kechikib. Yo‘lning yarmida mashinamiz buzilib qoldi. Oxir-oqibat, aynan o‘z vaqtida yetib bordik.

scenes.title: Hikoyadagi uchta o‘tgan zamon
board: Past simple → main events (the projector died)
Past continuous → background (managers were sitting)
Past perfect → earlier events (I had prepared for weeks)
scenes.say_native: Ikkinchi mavzu: vaqtni tartiblash. Past simple asosiy voqealar zanjirini beradi: died, picked up, drew. Past continuous fonni yaratadi: o‘sha paytda nima davom etayotgan edi. Past perfect esa hikoya vaqtidan oldinroq bo‘lgan narsani bildiradi, xuddi o‘zbekchadagi “tayyorlangan edim” kabi.
scenes.say: Use the past simple for the main events, the past continuous for the background, and the past perfect for things that happened even earlier.
scenes.say_uz: Asosiy voqealar uchun past simple, fon uchun past continuous, undan ham oldinroq bo‘lgan narsalar uchun past perfect ishlating.

scenes.title: When, while va by the time
board: was + -ing … when + past simple (bo‘lib turgan ish to‘xtatildi)
While I was waiting, … (davom etayotgan fon)
By the time I arrived, the meeting had started.

examples.t: I was walking to the office when my phone rang.
examples.uz: Ofisga piyoda ketayotgan edim, telefonim jiringlab qoldi.

examples.t: While I was waiting for the bus, I checked my notes.
By the time I got there, the meeting had already started.
examples.uz: Men yetib borgunimcha yig‘ilish allaqachon boshlangan edi.

scenes.say_native: “When” odatda qisqa, kutilmagan voqeani kiritadi va past simple bilan keladi: telefon jiringladi. “While” esa uzoqroq fonni kiritadi, ko‘pincha past continuous bilan. “By the time” dan keyin past simple, asosiy gapda esa past perfect keladi: men kelgunimcha yig‘ilish boshlanib bo‘lgan edi.
scenes.say: I was walking to the office when my phone rang. While I was waiting for the bus, I checked my notes. By the time I got there, the meeting had already started.
scenes.say_uz: Ofisga ketayotgan edim, telefonim jiringladi. Avtobus kutayotganimda yozuvlarimni ko‘rib chiqdim. Men yetib borgunimcha yig‘ilish allaqachon boshlangan edi.

scenes.title: Ketma-ketlik so‘zlari
board: First, … Then, … After that, …
As soon as I arrived, … (kelishim bilanoq)
Meanwhile, … (shu orada)
Eventually / In the end (oxir-oqibat)

examples.t: As soon as I saw the email, I called my manager.
examples.uz: Xatni ko‘rishim bilanoq rahbarimga qo‘ng‘iroq qildim.

examples.t: Meanwhile, my colleague was talking to the client.
examples.uz: Shu orada hamkasbim mijoz bilan gaplashayotgan edi.

scenes.say_native: Ketma-ketlik so‘zlari tinglovchiga xarita beradi. “As soon as” ikki voqea orasida deyarli vaqt yo‘qligini bildiradi. “Meanwhile” bir vaqtning o‘zida boshqa joyda nima bo‘layotganini ko‘rsatadi. “Eventually” va “in the end” esa uzoq kutish yoki qiyinchilikdan keyingi natijani bildiradi.
scenes.say: As soon as I saw the email, I called my manager. Meanwhile, my colleague was talking to the client. Eventually, we found a solution.
scenes.say_uz: Xatni ko‘rishim bilanoq rahbarimga qo‘ng‘iroq qildim. Shu orada hamkasbim mijoz bilan gaplashayotgan edi. Oxir-oqibat yechim topdik.

scenes.title: First yoki at first? In the end yoki at the end?
board: ✗ At first, I booked a taxi. Then I packed.
✓ First, I booked a taxi. Then I packed.
✗ After, we went home. ✓ After that / Afterwards, we went home.
At first = boshida (keyin o‘zgardi) · at the end of = …ning oxirida
scenes.say_native: Bu juftliklar ko‘p chalkashtiriladi. “First” ro‘yxatdagi birinchi qadam. “At first” esa “boshida shunday edi, keyin o‘zgardi” degani. “In the end” oxir-oqibat, “at the end of” esa biror narsaning oxirida: “at the end of the meeting”. Gap boshida yolg‘iz “After” demang, “After that” yoki “Afterwards” deng.
scenes.say: At first I hated the job, but later I loved it. First, I booked a taxi. At the end of the meeting, we took a photo. Afterwards, we went home.
scenes.say_uz: Boshida ishni yomon ko‘rardim, keyinroq esa yaxshi ko‘rib qoldim. Birinchi navbatda taksi buyurtma qildim. Yig‘ilish oxirida rasmga tushdik. Keyin uyga ketdik.

scenes.title: Zamonlardagi odatiy xatolar
board: ✗ When I arrived, they already left.
✓ When I arrived, they had already left.
✗ I was sleep when he called.
✓ I was sleeping when he called.
scenes.say_native: Ikki xato juda ko‘p uchraydi. Birinchisi: oldinroq bo‘lgan voqea uchun past perfect ishlatmaslik. Ular siz kelishdan oldin ketgan bo‘lsa, “they had already left”, xuddi “ketib bo‘lgan edi” kabi. Ikkinchisi: past continuous da “-ing” ni tushirib qoldirish. To‘g‘risi: was yoki were, keyin fe’l va “-ing”.
scenes.say: When I arrived, they had already left. I was sleeping when he called. We were having lunch when the fire alarm went off.
scenes.say_uz: Men kelganimda ular allaqachon ketib bo‘lgan edi. U qo‘ng‘iroq qilganda uxlayotgan edim. Yong‘in signali chalinganda tushlik qilayotgan edik.

scenes.title: Mashq: to‘g‘ri zamonni tanlang
board: 1 I ___ (work) late when the alarm went off.
2 By the time we reached the station, the train ___ (leave).
3 She ___ (open) the email and screamed.
4 While we ___ (wait), the boss walked in.
scenes.say_native: Qavs ichidagi fe’lni to‘g‘ri zamonga qo‘ying. O‘zingizdan so‘rang: bu asosiy voqeami, fonmi yoki undan ham oldinroq bo‘lgan narsami? Ikkinchi gapda “by the time” bor, uchinchisida esa ikki voqea ketma-ket sodir bo‘lgan. Javoblarni to‘liq gap bilan, baland ovozda ayting.
scenes.say: Put the verbs in the correct past tense. Ask yourself: is it a main event, the background, or something that happened earlier?
scenes.say_uz: Fe’llarni to‘g‘ri o‘tgan zamonga qo‘ying. O‘zingizdan so‘rang: bu asosiy voqeami, fonmi yoki oldinroq sodir bo‘lgan narsami?

scenes.title: Javoblar: zamonlar
board: 1 was working
2 had left
3 opened
4 were waiting
scenes.say_native: Birinchi: “was working”, ish davom etayotgan edi va signal uni bo‘ldi. Ikkinchi: “had left”, poyezd biz yetib borishdan oldin ketgan. Uchinchi: “opened”, ikki ketma-ket asosiy voqea, ikkalasi ham past simple. To‘rtinchi: “were waiting”, chunki “we” bilan “were” keladi. To‘rttasi to‘g‘ri bo‘lsa, a’lo.
scenes.say: One: I was working late when the alarm went off. Two: the train had left. Three: she opened the email and screamed. Four: while we were waiting, the boss walked in.
scenes.say_uz: Bir: signal chalinganda kech soatgacha ishlayotgan edim. Ikki: poyezd ketib bo‘lgan edi. Uch: u xatni ochdi va qichqirib yubordi. To‘rt: biz kutayotganimizda rahbar kirib keldi.

scenes.title: Mashq: ketma-ketlik so‘zini tanlang
board: 1 ___ I didn’t like London, but now I love it. (First / At first)
2 We waited for hours. ___ the plane took off. (Eventually / Meanwhile)
3 ___ I got home, I called my mum. (As soon as / After that)
4 We took a photo ___ the conference. (in the end / at the end of)
scenes.say_native: Endi qavs ichidagi ikki variantdan birini tanlang. Ma’noga qarang: fikr keyin o‘zgarganmi, uzoq kutishdan keyingi natijami, ikki voqea orasida vaqt bormi yoki tadbirning oxirgi qismi haqida gap ketyaptimi. Javoblarni to‘liq gap bilan ayting, so‘ngra mening javoblarim bilan solishtiring.
scenes.say: Choose the right linking word in each sentence. Think about the meaning, not just the grammar.
scenes.say_uz: Har bir gapda to‘g‘ri bog‘lovchi so‘zni tanlang. Faqat grammatikani emas, ma’noni ham o‘ylang.

scenes.title: Javoblar: ketma-ketlik so‘zlari
board: 1 At first (boshida, keyin o‘zgardi)
2 Eventually (uzoq kutishdan keyin)
3 As soon as (darhol)
4 at the end of (tadbirning oxirida)
scenes.say_native: Birinchi: “At first”, chunki fikr keyin o‘zgargan. Ikkinchi: “Eventually”, soatlab kutishdan keyingi natija; “meanwhile” mos emas, chunki parallel voqea yo‘q. Uchinchi: “As soon as I got home”; “after that” esa alohida turadi va undan keyin vergul keladi. To‘rtinchi: “at the end of the conference”.
scenes.say: At first I didn’t like London. Eventually, the plane took off. As soon as I got home, I called my mum. We took a photo at the end of the conference.
scenes.say_uz: Boshida Londonni yoqtirmagandim. Oxir-oqibat samolyot uchdi. Uyga kelishim bilanoq onamga qo‘ng‘iroq qildim. Konferensiya oxirida rasmga tushdik.

scenes.title: Dialog 1: dushanba ertalab ofisda
board: Mark · Dilnoza (colleagues)
Listen: What went wrong? How did it end?
scenes.say_native: Birinchi dialog. Dushanba ertalab ofis oshxonasida Mark hamkasbi Dilnozaga Berlinga safari haqida gapirib beradi. Ikki narsaga e’tibor bering: Mark zamonlar va ketma-ketlik so‘zlarini qanday ishlatyapti, Dilnoza esa hikoyani qanday reaksiyalar bilan qo‘llab-quvvatlayapti.
scenes.say: Mark: You won’t believe what happened on my way to Berlin. Dilnoza: Oh no, what happened? Mark: My first flight was late, so by the time we landed in Istanbul, my connection had already left. Dilnoza: Seriously? So what did you do? Mark: I spent four hours at the transfer desk. Eventually, I got a seat on the evening flight. But my suitcase didn’t arrive with me. Dilnoza: No way! What about your talk? Mark: I gave it in jeans and a hoodie. In the end, people loved it!
scenes.say_uz: Mark: Berlinga ketayotganimda nima bo‘lganiga ishonmaysiz. Dilnoza: Voy, nima bo‘ldi? Mark: Birinchi reysim kechikdi, Istanbulga qo‘nganimizda ulanadigan reysim allaqachon uchib ketgan edi. Dilnoza: Rostdanmi? Xo‘sh, nima qildingiz? Mark: Transfer stoykasida to‘rt soat o‘tkazdim. Oxir-oqibat kechki reysga joy oldim. Lekin chamadonim men bilan birga kelmadi. Dilnoza: Nahotki! Chiqishingiz-chi? Mark: Jinsi shim va kapyushonli kofta bilan chiqdim. Oxir-oqibat odamlarga juda yoqdi!

scenes.title: Mashq: dialog 1 savollari
board: 1 Why did Mark miss his connection?
2 How long did he spend at the transfer desk?
3 What didn’t arrive with him?
4 Which three reactions did Dilnoza use?
scenes.say_native: Dialogni eslab, to‘rtta savolga javob bering. Birinchi uchtasi faktlar haqida. To‘rtinchisi tinglovchining tili haqida: Dilnoza Markning hikoyasiga qaysi iboralar bilan munosabat bildirdi? To‘liq gap ishlatishga harakat qiling, masalan “He missed it because…”.
scenes.say: Answer the four questions about the conversation. For question four, try to remember Dilnoza’s exact words.
scenes.say_uz: Suhbat bo‘yicha to‘rtta savolga javob bering. To‘rtinchi savol uchun Dilnozaning aynan aytgan so‘zlarini eslashga harakat qiling.

scenes.title: Javoblar: dialog 1
board: 1 His first flight was late.
2 Four hours
3 His suitcase
4 Oh no! / Seriously? / No way!
scenes.say_native: Birinchi: birinchi reysi kechikkani uchun; “by the time we landed, my connection had already left”, yana past perfect. Ikkinchi: to‘rt soat. Uchinchi: chamadoni. To‘rtinchi: “Oh no”, “Seriously?” va “No way!”. Dilnoza yana “So what did you do?” deb so‘radi. Aynan shunday savollar hikoyani oldinga suradi.
scenes.say: He missed his connection because his first flight was late. He spent four hours at the desk, and his suitcase didn’t arrive. Dilnoza said: Oh no, Seriously, and No way.
scenes.say_uz: Birinchi reysi kechikkani uchun ulanadigan reysdan qoldi. Stoykada to‘rt soat o‘tkazdi, chamadoni esa kelmadi. Dilnoza: Voy, Rostdanmi va Nahotki dedi.

scenes.title: His-tuyg‘u: -ed va -ing sifatlar
board: I was exhausted / relieved / embarrassed. (mening holatim)
The flight was exhausting. (narsaning ta’siri)
I was bored. ≠ I was boring.

examples.t: I was so relieved when they found my bag.
The whole situation was really embarrassing.

scenes.say_native: Uchinchi mavzu: his-tuyg‘u qo‘shish. Tinglovchi faktlarnigina emas, siz nimani his qilganingizni ham bilmoqchi. “-ed” sifat insonning holatini bildiradi: “I was exhausted”. “-ing” esa vaziyatning ta’sirini: “The flight was exhausting.” “I was boring” desangiz, “men zerikarli odam edim” degan ma’no chiqadi.
scenes.say: Use -ed adjectives for how you felt and -ing adjectives for the thing that caused the feeling. I was exhausted because the flight was exhausting.
scenes.say_uz: O‘zingiz nimani his qilganingiz uchun -ed sifatlarni, o‘sha tuyg‘uni keltirib chiqargan narsa uchun -ing sifatlarni ishlating. Parvoz juda charchatuvchi bo‘lgani uchun holdan toygan edim.

scenes.title: Kuchli sifatlar
board: very tired → absolutely exhausted
very scared → terrified
very angry → furious
very happy → delighted / over the moon

examples.t: I was absolutely terrified before the interview.
examples.uz: Intervyudan oldin juda qo‘rqib ketgan edim.

examples.t: My manager was furious about the delay.

scenes.say_native: Hikoyani jonlantirishning eng oson yo‘li “very” o‘rniga kuchli sifat ishlatish: “exhausted”, “terrified”, “furious”. Muhim qoida: bunday kuchli sifat oldidan “very” emas, “absolutely”, “completely” yoki “really” keladi. “Over the moon” esa so‘zlashuvda “behad xursand” degani.
scenes.say: Strong adjectives make a story come alive. I was absolutely terrified before the interview. My manager was furious. When I got the offer, I was over the moon.
scenes.say_uz: Kuchli sifatlar hikoyani jonlantiradi. Intervyudan oldin dahshatli qo‘rqib ketgandim. Rahbarim qattiq g‘azablandi. Taklifni olganimda behad xursand bo‘ldim.

scenes.title: His-tuyg‘u so‘zlaridagi xatolar
board: ✗ I was very terrified. ✓ I was absolutely terrified.
✗ It was so embarrassed. ✓ It was so embarrassing.
✗ I felt myself bad. ✓ I felt terrible.
scenes.say_native: Uchta xato. “Very terrified” emas, “absolutely terrified”. Vaziyat “embarrassing”, siz esa “embarrassed” bo‘lasiz. Uchinchisi rus tilidan kelgan “I felt myself bad”, ya’ni “чувствовал себя плохо” ning tarjimasi. Ingliz tilida “myself” kerak emas: “I felt terrible” yoki “I didn’t feel well”.
scenes.say: I was absolutely terrified. It was so embarrassing. I felt terrible, and I didn’t feel well for the rest of the day.
scenes.say_uz: Dahshatli qo‘rqib ketgandim. Bu juda xijolatli edi. O‘zimni juda yomon his qildim va kunning qolgan qismida tobim bo‘lmadi.

scenes.title: Tafsilot va to‘g‘ridan-to‘g‘ri nutq
board: Luckily / Unfortunately / To my surprise, …
All of a sudden, the lights went out.
She looked at me and said, “Is this a joke?”
My hands were shaking. (kichik jonli tafsilot)

examples.t: To my surprise, the CEO was standing behind me.
examples.uz: Hayron qolganim shu bo‘ldiki, bosh direktor orqamda turgan ekan.

scenes.say_native: Yaxshi hikoyachi kichik jonli tafsilot beradi: titrayotgan qo‘llar, jim bo‘lib qolgan xona. “Luckily”, “unfortunately”, “to my surprise” voqeaga munosabatingizni ko‘rsatadi. Eng keskin lahzada esa to‘g‘ridan-to‘g‘ri nutq ishlating: “She looked at me and said…”. U ko‘chirma gapdan ancha jonliroq eshitiladi.
scenes.say: All of a sudden, the lights went out. My hands were shaking. Luckily, my colleague had a torch. Then the director looked at me and said, “Is this part of your presentation?”
scenes.say_uz: Birdaniga chiroqlar o‘chib qoldi. Qo‘llarim titrardi. Baxtimga, hamkasbimda chiroq bor ekan. Keyin direktor menga qarab: “Bu ham taqdimotingizning bir qismimi?” dedi.

scenes.title: Mashq: quruq hikoyani jonlantiring
board: Flat: I went to the bank. It was bad. I was very angry. Then it was OK.
Add: a time · a strong adjective · a detail · Luckily / In the end
scenes.say_native: Doskadagi hikoya juda quruq. Uni to‘rt-besh gapda qayta ayting. Vaqt qo‘shing, masalan “last Friday”. “Very angry” o‘rniga kuchli sifat ishlating. Bitta jonli tafsilot qo‘shing va oxirini “luckily” yoki “in the end” bilan yakunlang. Keyin mening variantim bilan solishtiring.
scenes.say: Make this flat story come alive. Add a time, a strong adjective, one vivid detail, and a clear ending.
scenes.say_uz: Bu quruq hikoyani jonlantiring. Vaqt, kuchli sifat, bitta jonli tafsilot va aniq yakun qo‘shing.

scenes.title: Namuna javob: bankdagi voqea
board: Last Friday, I went to the bank to pay my rent.
The queue was moving incredibly slowly, and I was furious.
All of a sudden, a new window opened.
In the end, I was out in five minutes.
scenes.say_native: Mana mumkin bo‘lgan variant. Vaqt bor: “last Friday”. Maqsad bor: ijara haqini to‘lash. Kuchli sifat bor: “furious”. Burilish nuqtasi “all of a sudden” bilan keldi, yakun esa “in the end” bilan. Sizning variantingiz boshqacha bo‘lishi tabiiy, asosiysi shu to‘rt element bo‘lsin.
scenes.say: Last Friday, I went to the bank to pay my rent. The queue was moving incredibly slowly, and I was absolutely furious. All of a sudden, a new window opened right in front of me. In the end, I was out in five minutes.
scenes.say_uz: O‘tgan juma ijara haqini to‘lash uchun bankka bordim. Navbat juda sekin yurardi, men esa qattiq g‘azablangan edim. Birdaniga ro‘paramda yangi oyna ochildi. Oxir-oqibat besh daqiqada chiqib ketdim.

scenes.title: Mashq: to‘g‘ri so‘zni tanlang
board: 1 The meeting lasted three hours. I was ___ . (exhausted / exhausting)
2 I forgot the client’s name. It was so ___ . (embarrassed / embarrassing)
3 When I saw the bill, I was ___ furious. (very / absolutely)
4 ___ , the manager was in a good mood. (Luckily / Lucky)
scenes.say_native: To‘rtta qisqa gap. Qavs ichidagi ikki so‘zdan birini tanlang. Eslang: odamning holati “-ed”, vaziyatning ta’siri “-ing”. Kuchli sifat oldidan qaysi so‘z keladi? Oxirgi gapda esa butun gapga munosabat bildiradigan ravish kerak. Javoblarni to‘liq gap qilib ayting.
scenes.say: Choose the correct word in each sentence. Think about feelings, causes and strong adjectives.
scenes.say_uz: Har bir gapda to‘g‘ri so‘zni tanlang. His-tuyg‘u, sabab va kuchli sifatlar haqida o‘ylang.

scenes.title: Javoblar: his-tuyg‘u so‘zlari
board: 1 exhausted
2 embarrassing
3 absolutely
4 Luckily
scenes.say_native: Birinchi: “exhausted”, bu mening holatim. Ikkinchi: “embarrassing”, chunki gapda “it” bor, vaziyat xijolatli edi. Uchinchi: “absolutely furious”, “very” emas. To‘rtinchi: “Luckily”, ravish, butun gapga izoh beradi. “Lucky” esa sifat, u gap boshida vergul bilan yolg‘iz turolmaydi.
scenes.say: I was exhausted. It was so embarrassing. I was absolutely furious. Luckily, the manager was in a good mood.
scenes.say_uz: Holdan toygan edim. Bu juda xijolatli edi. Qattiq g‘azablangan edim. Baxtimga, rahbarning kayfiyati yaxshi edi.

scenes.title: Boshqalarning hikoyasiga munosabat
board: Surprise: Really? / No way! / You’re kidding!
Sympathy: Oh no! / That must have been awful.
Interest: What happened next? / So what did you do?
Joy: That’s brilliant! / Good for you!
scenes.say_native: To‘rtinchi mavzu: tinglovchi bo‘lish. Ingliz tilidagi suhbatda jim tinglash qiziqmaslik kabi tuyuladi. Hayratlansangiz “No way!”, achinsangiz “Oh no!”, qiziqsangiz “What happened next?”, xursand bo‘lsangiz “Good for you!” deng. Ohang ham muhim: keng, tepaga ko‘tariluvchi “Really?” chin qiziqishni bildiradi.
scenes.say: Good listeners react all the time. No way! You’re kidding! Oh no, that must have been awful. So what did you do next? That’s brilliant, good for you!
scenes.say_uz: Yaxshi tinglovchilar doim munosabat bildiradi. Nahotki! Hazillashyapsizmi! Voy, bu dahshatli bo‘lgan bo‘lsa kerak. Xo‘sh, keyin nima qildingiz? Zo‘r-ku, barakalla!

scenes.title: Must have been va qisqa savollar
board: That must have been scary. (o‘tgandagi holatga taxmin)
A: I lost my passport. B: Did you? Oh no!
A: We were stuck for hours. B: Were you? How awful!
scenes.say_native: Ikkita kuchli vosita. Birinchisi “must have been” va sifat: “That must have been scary”, ya’ni “qo‘rqinchli bo‘lgan bo‘lsa kerak”. Ikkinchisi qisqa aks savol: hikoyachining yordamchi fe’lini qaytarasiz. “I lost my passport” deyilsa “Did you?”, “We were stuck” deyilsa “Were you?”.
scenes.say: I lost my passport in Rome. Did you? Oh no, that must have been stressful. We were stuck in the lift for an hour. Were you? How awful!
scenes.say_uz: Rimda pasportimni yo‘qotib qo‘ydim. Shundaymi? Voy, bu juda asabiy bo‘lgan bo‘lsa kerak. Liftda bir soat qamalib qoldik. Shundaymi? Qanday dahshat!

scenes.title: Tinglovchining xatolari
board: ✗ It must be awful. (o‘tgan voqea uchun)
✓ It must have been awful.
✗ That’s nothing! When I… (hikoyani tortib olish)
✓ That reminds me of the time I…
scenes.say_native: Birinchi xato: tugagan voqea uchun “it must be awful” deyish; kerakli shakl “must have been”. Ikkinchisi: jim o‘tirish yoki tekis ohangda “yes, yes” deyish. Uchinchisi: birovning hikoyasini “That’s nothing!” deb kesish. O‘xshash hikoyangiz bo‘lsa, avval munosabat bildiring, keyin “That reminds me of the time…” deng.
scenes.say: Oh no, that must have been awful. I’m glad it ended well. Actually, that reminds me of the time I missed my own birthday party.
scenes.say_uz: Voy, bu dahshatli bo‘lgan bo‘lsa kerak. Yaxshi tugaganidan xursandman. Aytgancha, bu menga o‘z tug‘ilgan kunimdagi ziyofatga ulgurmay qolganimni eslatdi.

scenes.title: Mashq: hikoyaga munosabat bildiring
board: 1 “My laptop died the night before my deadline.”
2 “I got the job!”
3 “I was lost in Istanbul airport for two hours.”
4 “Guess who I met at the conference? The CEO!”
scenes.say_native: To‘rtta gapga tez va tabiiy munosabat bildiring. Har biriga ikki qismli javob tuzing: avval qisqa reaksiya, keyin savol yoki “must have been” bilan gap. Ohangga ham e’tibor bering: hayrat va quvonch keng, tepaga ko‘tariluvchi ohangni talab qiladi, hamdardlik esa yumshoqroq ohangni.
scenes.say: React to each line with a short reaction plus a follow-up question or a must have been sentence.
scenes.say_uz: Har bir gapga qisqa reaksiya va qo‘shimcha savol yoki must have been bilan gap orqali munosabat bildiring.

scenes.title: Javob namunalari: reaksiyalar
board: 1 Oh no! That must have been so stressful. What did you do?
2 That’s brilliant! Congratulations! When do you start?
3 Were you? That must have been awful.
4 No way! What did you talk about?
scenes.say_native: Kompyuter buzilgan bo‘lsa, hamdardlik va savol: “That must have been so stressful.” Ishga qabul qilingan bo‘lsa, tabrik va “When do you start?” Uchinchi gapda “Were you?” tabiiy, chunki gapda “was” bor. To‘rtinchisida “No way!” va qiziqish savoli. Javobingiz shu tuzilmada bo‘lsa, a’lo.
scenes.say: Oh no! That must have been so stressful. That’s brilliant, congratulations! When do you start? Were you? That must have been awful. No way! What did you talk about?
scenes.say_uz: Voy! Bu juda asabiy bo‘lgan bo‘lsa kerak. Zo‘r-ku, tabriklayman! Qachon boshlaysiz? Shundaymi? Bu dahshatli bo‘lgan bo‘lsa kerak. Nahotki! Nima haqida gaplashdingiz?

scenes.title: Dialog 2: ish suhbatidagi hikoya
board: Interviewer · Bekzod (candidate)
“Tell me about a time something went wrong.”
Listen: job · problem · action · result
scenes.say_native: Ikkinchi dialog jiddiyroq: ish suhbati. Intervyu oluvchi Bekzoddan ishda biror narsa noto‘g‘ri ketgan holat haqida so‘raydi. STAR usulini eslang: vaziyat, vazifa, harakat, natija. Tinglab, Bekzodning hikoyasida shu qismlarni toping va zamonlarga e’tibor bering.
scenes.say: Interviewer: Can you tell me about a time when something went wrong at work? Bekzod: Sure. Last year I was working as a project coordinator at a logistics company. Two days before a big client visit, we found out that the demo equipment had been sent to the wrong city. I was really worried, because the client was considering a three-year contract. So I called several local suppliers, and eventually I found one that could rent us the same equipment. In the end, the visit went smoothly and we signed the contract.
scenes.say_uz: Intervyu oluvchi: Ishda biror narsa noto‘g‘ri ketgan holat haqida gapirib bera olasizmi? Bekzod: Albatta. O‘tgan yili logistika kompaniyasida loyiha koordinatori bo‘lib ishlayotgan edim. Muhim mijoz tashrifidan ikki kun oldin namoyish uskunalari boshqa shaharga jo‘natib yuborilganini bilib qoldik. Juda xavotirlandim, chunki mijoz uch yillik shartnomani ko‘rib chiqayotgan edi. Shuning uchun bir nechta mahalliy yetkazib beruvchilarga qo‘ng‘iroq qildim va oxir-oqibat bizga xuddi shunday uskunani ijaraga bera oladiganini topdim. Natijada tashrif silliq o‘tdi va shartnomani imzoladik.

scenes.title: Mashq: dialog 2 savollari
board: 1 What was Bekzod’s job?
2 What went wrong?
3 What did he do about it?
4 What was the result?
scenes.say_native: To‘rtta savol STAR qismlariga mos keladi: vaziyat, muammo, harakat va natija. Ikkinchi savolga javob berganda grammatikaga e’tibor bering: Bekzod uskunaning noto‘g‘ri yuborilganini qaysi shakl bilan aytdi? Javoblarni qisqa, lekin to‘liq gaplar bilan ayting.
scenes.say: Answer the four questions. Notice how each answer matches one part of the STAR method.
scenes.say_uz: To‘rtta savolga javob bering. Har bir javob STAR usulining bir qismiga mos kelishiga e’tibor bering.

scenes.title: Javoblar: dialog 2
board: 1 Project coordinator at a logistics company
2 The equipment had been sent to the wrong city.
3 He called local suppliers and rented the same equipment.
4 The visit went smoothly; they signed the contract.
scenes.say_native: Javoblar: loyiha koordinatori; uskuna boshqa shaharga jo‘natilgan edi, “had been sent”; mahalliy yetkazib beruvchidan ijaraga oldi; shartnoma imzolandi. E’tibor bering, Bekzod “I called”, “I found” deydi. Biz kamtarlik uchun ko‘pincha “biz” deymiz, lekin intervyuda o‘z hissangizni “I” bilan ayting.
scenes.say: I was a project coordinator. The equipment had been sent to the wrong city. I called local suppliers, I found the same equipment, and in the end we signed the contract.
scenes.say_uz: Men loyiha koordinatori edim. Uskuna noto‘g‘ri shaharga jo‘natilgan edi. Men mahalliy yetkazib beruvchilarga qo‘ng‘iroq qildim, xuddi shunday uskunani topdim va oxir-oqibat shartnomani imzoladik.

scenes.title: Talaffuz: -ed ning uch xil o‘qilishi
board: /ɪd/ after t, d: waited, decided
/t/ after p, k, f, s, ʃ, tʃ: stopped, worked, laughed
/d/ after other sounds: arrived, happened, called
scenes.say_native: Hikoyada o‘tgan zamon fe’llari ko‘p, shuning uchun “-ed” talaffuzi muhim. Fe’l “t” yoki “d” tovushi bilan tugasa, yangi bo‘g‘in qo‘shiladi: “waited”. Jarangsiz tovushdan keyin “t” eshitiladi: “stopped”, “worked”. Qolgan holatlarda “d”: “arrived”. Ko‘pchilik har doim “work-ed” deb o‘qiydi, bu xato.
scenes.say: Waited, decided. Stopped, worked, laughed. Arrived, happened, called. Worked has one syllable, not two.
scenes.say_uz: Kutdi, qaror qildi. To‘xtadi, ishladi, kuldi. Yetib keldi, sodir bo‘ldi, qo‘ng‘iroq qildi. Worked bir bo‘g‘inli, ikki emas.

scenes.title: Mashq: -ed qanday o‘qiladi?
board: 1 needed · 2 asked
3 opened · 4 panicked
scenes.say_native: To‘rtta fe’l. Har biri uchun “-ed” qanday o‘qilishini ayting: “t”, “d” yoki “id”. Yozuvga emas, fe’lning oxirgi tovushiga qarang: “panic” “k” tovushi bilan tugaydi, “open” esa “n” bilan. Javob bergach, xuddi hikoyadagidek, har bir so‘zni baland ovozda talaffuz qiling.
scenes.say: How do you pronounce the ending of each verb? Choose t, d or id, then say the word aloud.
scenes.say_uz: Har bir fe’lning oxirini qanday talaffuz qilasiz? t, d yoki id ni tanlang, keyin so‘zni baland ovozda ayting.

scenes.title: Javoblar: -ed talaffuzi
board: 1 needed /ɪd/
2 asked /t/
3 opened /d/
4 panicked /t/
scenes.say_native: “Needed” “d” bilan tugaydi, shuning uchun qo‘shimcha bo‘g‘in: “need-id”. “Asked” jarangsiz “k” dan keyin “t”, bir bo‘g‘in. “Opened” “n” dan keyin “d”. “Panicked” yozuvda “ck” bor, tovush esa “k”, shuning uchun “t”. Yodda tuting: yozuvdagi harf emas, tovush hal qiladi.
scenes.say: Needed. Asked. Opened. Panicked. I panicked, asked for help, and needed ten minutes to calm down.
scenes.say_uz: Kerak bo‘ldi. So‘radi. Ochdi. Vahimaga tushdi. Men vahimaga tushdim, yordam so‘radim va tinchlanishim uchun o‘n daqiqa kerak bo‘ldi.

scenes.title: Yakuniy topshiriq: bir daqiqalik hikoya
board: Tell me about a time something went wrong.
Hook → background → turning point → ending + lesson
Use: was -ing when · had + V3 · eventually
Add: one strong adjective · one direct quote
scenes.say_native: Endi navbat sizga. Ishda, o‘qishda yoki safarda biror narsa noto‘g‘ri ketgan holat haqida bir daqiqa gapiring. Doskadagi tartibga amal qiling, past continuous, past perfect va “eventually” yoki “in the end” ishlating. Bitta kuchli sifat va bitta to‘g‘ridan-to‘g‘ri gap qo‘shing. Taymerni yoqing.
scenes.say: Your turn. Tell a one-minute story about a time something went wrong. Start with a hook and finish with what you learned.
scenes.say_uz: Navbat sizga. Biror narsa noto‘g‘ri ketgan holat haqida bir daqiqalik hikoya aytib bering. Hook bilan boshlang va nima o‘rganganingiz bilan yakunlang.

scenes.title: Namuna javob: noto‘g‘ri xat
board: I’ll never forget my first week at the bank.
I was answering emails when I noticed…
I’d sent the report to the wrong client!
What I learned was to check every address twice.
scenes.say_native: Mana namuna. Hook: birinchi ish haftasi. Fon past continuous bilan, burilish nuqtasi past perfect bilan: hisobot noto‘g‘ri mijozga ketgan. Kuchli sifat “horrified”, to‘g‘ridan-to‘g‘ri gap rahbarning so‘zlari, oxirida saboq. Hikoyangizni solishtiring: qaysi element yetishmadi, keyingi safar o‘shani qo‘shing.
scenes.say: I’ll never forget my first week at the bank. I was answering emails when I suddenly realised I’d sent a report to the wrong client. I was absolutely horrified. I went straight to my manager, and she said, “Thank you for telling me so quickly.” Luckily, the client deleted it. What I learned was to check every address twice.
scenes.say_uz: Bankdagi birinchi ish haftamni hech qachon unutmayman. Xatlarga javob yozayotgan edim, birdan hisobotni noto‘g‘ri mijozga yuborganimni angladim. Dahshatga tushdim. To‘g‘ri rahbarimning oldiga bordim, u esa: “Buni tezda aytganingiz uchun rahmat”, dedi. Baxtimga, mijoz uni o‘chirib tashladi. O‘rganganim shu bo‘ldiki, har bir manzilni ikki marta tekshirish kerak.

scenes.title: Xulosa: yaxshi hikoyaning to‘rt kaliti
board: Structure: hook → background → turning point → point
Tenses: past simple · past continuous · past perfect
Feelings: -ed/-ing, strong adjectives, direct speech
Reactions: No way! · That must have been… · Did you?
scenes.say_native: Xulosa. Hikoya hook bilan boshlanadi, qisqa fon, burilish nuqtasi va xulosa bilan tugaydi. Uch o‘tgan zamon vaqtni tartiblaydi. His-tuyg‘u uchun “-ed” sifatlar va kuchli sifatlar, keskin lahza uchun to‘g‘ridan-to‘g‘ri nutq. Tinglaganda esa “No way!”, “must have been” va qisqa savollar bilan munosabat bildiring.
scenes.say: You can now structure a story, sequence events clearly, add feelings and detail, and react naturally when someone else is telling a story.
scenes.say_uz: Endi siz hikoyani tuzib, voqealarni aniq tartiblay olasiz, his-tuyg‘u va tafsilot qo‘shasiz hamda boshqalar hikoya qilganda tabiiy munosabat bildirasiz.

scenes.title: Uy vazifasi va keyingi dars
board: Homework: record a 2-minute personal story
Check: hook · 3 past tenses · 2 feelings · a clear point
Listen back: -ed endings /t/ /d/ /ɪd/
scenes.say_native: Uy vazifasi: o‘zingiz bilan bo‘lgan haqiqiy voqea haqida ikki daqiqalik hikoyani yozib oling. Mezon: hook bor, uchta o‘tgan zamon ishlatilgan, kamida ikkita his-tuyg‘u so‘zi va aniq xulosa bor. Keyin yozuvni tinglab, “-ed” oxirlarini tekshiring. Keyingi darsda bahslashish va o‘z fikringizni himoya qilishni o‘rganamiz.
scenes.say: Record a two-minute story about something that really happened to you. Then listen back and check your structure, your tenses and your endings. See you next time!
scenes.say_uz: Siz bilan haqiqatan sodir bo‘lgan voqea haqida ikki daqiqalik hikoyani yozib oling. Keyin uni tinglab, tuzilma, zamonlar va qo‘shimchalarni tekshiring. Keyingi safar ko‘rishguncha!

homework_uz: O‘zingiz bilan bo‘lgan haqiqiy voqea (ishda, o‘qishda yoki safarda) haqida ikki daqiqalik hikoyani ovozli yozib oling. Muvaffaqiyat mezoni: hikoya hook bilan boshlanadi va aniq xulosa bilan tugaydi; past simple, past continuous va past perfect kamida bir martadan ishlatilgan; kamida ikkita his-tuyg‘u sifati (masalan, relieved, furious) va bitta to‘g‘ridan-to‘g‘ri gap bor. Yozuvni qayta tinglab, -ed oxirlari to‘g‘ri talaffuz qilinganini tekshiring.

quiz.q: Which sentence is the best hook for a story?
options: I want to tell you a story about my trip.
You won’t believe what happened on my trip.
Now I will speak about my trip.
quiz.why_uz: Hook tinglovchini qiziqtiradi; “I want to tell you a story about…” rasmiy e’lon kabi eshitiladi.

quiz.q: I ___ to the office when my phone rang.
quiz.why_uz: Bo‘lib turgan fon harakati past continuous bilan: was walking; “was walk” xato.

quiz.q: By the time we arrived, the meeting ___ .
quiz.why_uz: By the time dan keyin asosiy gapda oldinroq bo‘lgan voqea past perfect bilan: had already started.

quiz.q: ___ I hated the job, but later I loved it.
quiz.why_uz: At first = boshida (keyin o‘zgardi). First esa ketma-ketlikdagi birinchi qadam.

quiz.q: We waited for hours. ___, the plane took off.
quiz.why_uz: Uzoq kutishdan keyingi natija: eventually. At the end yolg‘iz bu ma’noda ishlatilmaydi.
Narsaning ta’siri -ing bilan: exhausting. Odamning holati esa exhausted.
Kuchli sifat bilan very emas, absolutely ishlatiladi.

quiz.q: Your friend says: “We were stuck in the lift for an hour.” The best reaction is:
options: Were you? That must have been awful.
quiz.why_uz: O‘tgan voqeaga hamdardlik: must have been; aks savol “Were you?” qiziqishni ko‘rsatadi.
Jarangsiz /k/ dan keyin -ed /t/ bo‘lib o‘qiladi: worked bir bo‘g‘inli.

quiz.q: Which sentence shows the speaker’s attitude to the event?
options: Luckily, my colleague had a spare laptop.
Lucky, my colleague had a spare laptop.
My colleague luckily had laptop spare.
quiz.why_uz: Luckily ravishi butun gapga munosabat bildiradi; lucky sifat gap boshida yolg‘iz kelmaydi.
